mechanism_narrative: A low and stable federal funds rate environment (below 0.5%) compresses the risk-free rate, reducing the discount rate for equity valuations and driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS remains below 0.5% for 3 consecutive months but S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of such periods.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 5.0% signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which typically precedes a recession and causes negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate reduced corporate earnings.
failure_condition: When UNRATE > 5.0, S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of cases over the last 5 years.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in consumer spending (RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) indicate a broad-based weakening in demand, which triggers a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 trading days as the market prices in reduced economic activity.
failure_condition: The joint decline in RSAFS and HOUST (both down > 1% MoM) occurs but S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of such instances.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of declining industrial production (INDPRO < 105.0) and rising manufacturing inventories, the S&P 500 tends to underperform by -0.5% over the next 60 trading days as supply chain disruptions and weak output signal a slowing economy.
failure_condition: When INDPRO < 105.0, S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of cases over the last 5 years.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in the core inflation rate (CPIAUCSL) above 3.5% signals persistent inflation, prompting the Federal Reserve to tighten monetary policy and causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When CPIAUCSL > 3.5, S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of cases over the last 5 years.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in consumer spending (RSAFS) above its 12-month moving average indicates robust economic activity, which supports corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: RSAFS remains above its 12-month moving average for 3 consecutive months but S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of such periods.

mechanism_narrative: In a low-unemployment regime (UNRATE < 4.0%), a rising labor force participation rate (PAYEMS growth > 0.5% MoM) signals labor market tightness, which typically leads to wage inflation and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as the market anticipates higher corporate profits.
failure_condition: When UNRATE < 4.0 and PAYEMS growth > 0.5% MoM, S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of cases over the last 5 years.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in industrial production (INDPRO) and a rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates a weakening economy with both supply constraints and labor market stress, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: When INDPRO declines and UNRATE rises (both > 0.5% MoM change), S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of such instances.
